release.title: Kima Hub 1.24.1 — Reliable Library Scans
release.summary: Keep importing readable music when an individual folder denies access, preserve existing library records, and remove retired Downtify scanqueue code.

items.title: Library refresh keeps going
items.summary: A blocked subfolder no longer stops the entire music scan.
items.body: The library scanner now continues through readable artist and album folders when a nested directory denies access (EACCES or EPERM). This lets new Lidarr or Soulseek music appear without waiting for unrelated legacy import-folder permissions to be fixed. A blocked music root or unexpected I/O failure still stops the scan to protect the library.

items.title: Preserve music history during partial scans
items.summary: Unreachable tracks are not mistaken for deleted files.
items.body: Tracks inside a skipped unreadable subtree keep their existing library records and missing-file status. A manually started scan finishes with a visible warning naming the inaccessible folder instead of silently reporting a clean run. Administrators can fix filesystem permissions without deleting music or losing existing history.

items.title: Remove old Downtify scanqueue hooks
items.summary: Retired integration code no longer participates in scan job IDs.
items.body: The discontinued Downtify-specific scan request field and its obsolete tests are removed. Normal Lidarr, Soulseek and full-library refresh requests remain supported. Historical database migrations and music files remain untouched for safe upgrades and backups.

titles.Kima Hub 1.24.1 — Reliable Library Scans: Kima Hub 1.24.1 — Betrouwbaar scannen van de muziekbibliotheek

summaries.Keep importing readable music when an in: Blijf leesbare muziek importeren als één map geen toegang geeft, behoud bestaande bibliotheekgegevens en verwijder verouderde Downtify-scanqueue-code.

fork.1241.scan-permissions.title: Bibliotheek verversen gaat verder
fork.1241.scan-permissions.summary: Een geblokkeerde submap stopt niet langer de volledige muziekscan.
fork.1241.scan-permissions.body: De bibliotheekscanner verwerkt nu gewoon leesbare artiest- en albummappen als een onderliggende map de toegang weigert (EACCES of EPERM). Nieuwe muziek van Lidarr of Soulseek kan daardoor verschijnen zonder te wachten op herstel van rechten in een oude importmap. Als de hoofdmap onleesbaar is of een onverwachte I/O-fout optreedt, stopt de scan nog steeds om de bibliotheek te beschermen.

fork.1241.keep-history.title: Behoud geschiedenis bij gedeeltelijke scans
fork.1241.keep-history.summary: Ontoegankelijke nummers worden niet als verwijderd beschouwd.
fork.1241.keep-history.body: Nummers in een overgeslagen, onleesbare submap behouden hun bestaande bibliotheekregistratie en status. Een handmatige scan wordt afgerond met een duidelijke waarschuwing die de ontoegankelijke map noemt, in plaats van stilzwijgend succes te melden. Beheerders kunnen de bestandsrechten herstellen zonder muziek of bestaande geschiedenis te wissen.

fork.1241.legacy-cleanup.title: Oude Downtify-scanqueue-code opgeruimd
fork.1241.legacy-cleanup.summary: De verwijderde integratie maakt geen eigen scanopdrachten meer aan.
fork.1241.legacy-cleanup.body: Het ongebruikte Downtify-veld voor scanverzoeken en de bijbehorende oude tests zijn verwijderd. Gewone Lidarr-, Soulseek- en volledige bibliotheekscans blijven ondersteund. Historische databasemigraties en muziekbestanden blijven behouden voor veilige upgrades en back-ups.

changelog:
A targeted maintenance release for the OxygenGS fork after user-reported EACCES failures in old Singles folders blocked new Lidarr music. Keep the current app independently configurable and retain the published v1.24.0 image as the production default until v1.24.1 passes its own stable-release gates.

### Partial scans without losing existing music
- PR #252: treat EACCES/EPERM on nested real music directories as a documented partial scan. Continue indexing files in readable branches; never silently discard the failure.
- Do not treat tracks in an unreadable subtree as missing: preserve track records, playlists, play history, artist/album associations and the existing missing flag.
- Keep an unreadable library root or unexpected filesystem I/O errors fatal to avoid falsely treating inaccessible storage as deleted.
- Update manual scan notifications to report a warning and identify a blocked directory rather than displaying an unqualified success.
- Add regression coverage for inaccessible folders, fatal root and EIO errors, and fresh music appearing elsewhere while an existing library subtree remains inaccessible.

### Retire obsolete integration hooks
- PR #253: remove the discontinued Downtify-specific scanqueue request field, job ID branch and obsolete tests. Supported full-library, Lidarr, Soulseek, album and discovery scans remain unchanged.
- Preserve historical Prisma migration files and tables rather than destructively rewriting existing database migration history. Do not remove, move or chmod any user music.

### Documentation and build workflow cleanup
- PR #251: refresh the public README, installation examples, changelog, security report and versioned Compose defaults for the published v1.24.0 baseline.
- Retire four redundant, manual or duplicate GitHub Actions definitions while keeping mandatory source tests, security checks, native AMD64/ARM64 image builds and explicit stable-release approval.
- The individual changes were merged only after complete source/compatibility/security/native AIO checks passed. This candidate requires its own full CI and exact-main native-image preflight before any stable tag, GitHub Release or Docker image may be published.

### Safe installation and remaining risks
- No new database migration, external service, download protocol, storage mount or media operation is introduced by this patch.
- A scanner warning means some media is inaccessible; correct the actual host and container permissions to index those files. The patch does not change or bypass permissions.
- Keep the existing Compose project identity and music/download mounts. Create and verify a restorable cold backup of the complete /data volume before any live upgrade.
- Prior native AIO images had unresolved HIGH/CRITICAL advisories; a green build is not a zero-vulnerability claim. Review new architecture-specific scan evidence before approving a release.
